book_title: Creativity in the Unified Field - Book of Exercises & Practices
author: Richard Moon

exercises.title: DropBackSinkOpen (DBSO)
exercises.meta: Solo · 30 sec, repeated through the day
exercises.body:
Whenever you notice tension, a fixed idea, or a reactive moment: drop back, sink, open. If you re-tighten, release again — in ever-finer increments, anywhere, any time.

This is the foundation everything else rests on. 'Calm the spirit. Return to the source.' Once in the morning is not enough — KeepDoingIt.

exercises.title: listen to the impulse to breathe
exercises.meta: Solo · 2–4 min · after DBSO · the reverse movement of the five-stage breath
exercises.body:
after dropping back, sinking, and opening, don't take the breath — wait for it. feel the impulse to breathe arise on its own, and let it breathe you.

rather than running the breath, feel life activating it — the universal pulse breathing you. this is the reverse of Breathing the Whole System, met here as an early taste right after DropBackSinkOpen.

exercises.title: Feel / Locate / Align / Unify (Kamae)
exercises.meta: Solo · 3–5 min · Create A Beautiful World in 3 Aikido Lessons
exercises.body:
Feel and locate the central core of your being. Feel the 'glow of life' that is you. Apply DBSO in ever-finer alignment.

Notice that each small shift in the location of attention creates a different experiential world.

exercises.title: Tense & Release Body Scan (Align, Allow, Appreciate)
exercises.body:
Gently tense the whole body, then relax and feel. Re-tense the muscles progressively closer to the spine, head to hips, releasing each time.

As you relax, feel into the central core of being — align with gravity, allow the tension to release, appreciate the flow. How long? As long as you're enjoying it.

exercises.title: Center of the Central Core Relaxation
exercises.body:
Move sequentially through the body's regions — mind, brain, forehead, eyes, jaw, throat, shoulders, abdomen, hips, legs, feet — sinking open into the 'gravity shadow' at each.

No fixed pace. A natural candidate for a longer recorded guided track and a fitting close to Part I.

exercises.title: Wrist Grab Grounding
exercises.meta: Partner · 5 min · Adventures in Aiki-land (R. Moon, 2010)
exercises.body:
A partner grabs your extended wrist and gently pushes, then pulls. Resisting the push lets them pull you easily, resisting the pull lets them push you; relaxing and 'feeling where you are' produces an effortless presence that is harder to move.

At first 50/50 - resist less, ground more. After a while the resistance becomes hard to see from outside but you feel it inside. Eventually 50% → 60% ground.

DBSO KeepDoingIt. Real or invisible partner.

alternate: Push — resisting lets them pull you easily — relax & feel where you are
Pull — resisting lets them push — relax & feel where you are

segments.prompt: Resistance hard to see from outside but you feel it inside

exercises.title: Lesson II — Breathe Universal Harmony (Aiki Kokyu)
exercises.meta: Solo · 3–5 min · Create A Beautiful World in 3 Aikido Lessons
exercises.body: Breathe in harmony so each cell 'enjoys life's glow.' The lesson that opens the whole-system view of breath — the second of the three Aikido Lessons, pairing with Lesson I.

exercises.title: Breathing the Whole System (Five-Stage Breath)
The O2 Continuum
exercises.body:
Feel where you are on the O2 continuum — from O2 debt, through perfect saturation, to reserve. Locate it consciously; sense which cells feel in balance and which don't.

Then breathe exactly the way you want for two or three breaths, and feel your location shift. It usually takes fewer than three; it never takes seven. First your own oxygen mask on first— then you have the reserves

-- create a beautiful world.

exercises.title: Ocean Breathing
exercises.body: Remember, or imagine, the first deep breath of ocean air — every cell lights up, the glow of life increases, and a natural desire for another breath follows. Breathe at the ocean even when you can't be there; hold the feeling.

exercises.title: Infant Breathing
exercises.body: Imagine breathing as an infant — oxygen equalized after birth, simply lying there breathing and enjoying the glow of life, no thought, no thing. A return to the purity of being before socialization.

exercises.title: Ten to the Tenth — State Shifting Scale
exercises.meta: Solo (can be coached) · 10–30 min to learn, seconds once trained · Ten to the Tenth
exercises.body:
Rate your current state 1–10. Notice why, by felt sense. 'Square away'your posture, breath, and attention until the number plateaus higher, then 'call up' the next number and embody it, on up to 10.

*Down the Scale (Contrast Step)*

*Solo · 1–2 min · Ten to the Tenth*

After climbing to  4, briefly imagine and feel dropping a number back to 3 then go to 6 then drop back to 4 — 6 to 5 to 4 — noticing the self-talk and physical contraction that come with it.

*Getting to 10*

7 should be feeling very capable.  10 will be your best operating place, entering flow state.

8 Remember a day when everything went fine, even the hard stuff

9 Remember one of those really great days that come back to you, good times with family, a great day at work

10 Think back to the best day you can remember.  Really soak in it move, breathe.  Think again when did you enter flow state and were able to be there for longer than made sense.  You were laughing joyously as the unsolvable situation just melted away

*Quantum Shift*

Rlabel 10 as a new '1' and climb again through octaves. Once trained, the whole move compresses to a near-instant cue. The most fully documented exercise in the source.

exercises.title: Enjoy / Joy / Appreciate
exercises.body:
Intentionally enjoy yourself — 'enjoy yourSELF enjoying joy.' Bring attention to something you love, and treat the enjoyment as guidance: 'feeling better' signals a useful direction. Close with DBSO.

Completes the Feel (I) / Breathe (II) / Enjoy (III) arc. It names Ki, but the practice itself is attention and appreciation — confirmed for Part III.

exercises.title: Shoulder Slap — Sensing Finer Dimensions
exercises.meta: Partner · 5–15 min · Aikido class teaching (R. Moon), cleaned · closes Part III
exercises.body:
A re-attacking slap on the shoulder in place of a shomen strike. Stance is flexible — natural stance (shizentai), a left- or right-foot lead all work; natural stance paired with the finger-snap is the simplest way in, and hanmi is fine in a dojo. Partners stand one step apart and agree on force: relaxed enough to sting a little, reality not fear, never to hurt.

*Attacker***.** Don't telegraph. Go from nothing to the hit as fast as you can — a real attack carries a burst of ki, and a slow or sloppy approach gives a different, weaker feel. Vary the timing; never count “one, two, three, slap.”

*Receiver***.** Start one step away. For the first few reps, snap your fingers the instant you sense the attack is about to come, then check — early, late, close? Come to center and face the attacker so you feel their attention. Give the most honest feedback you canProgress from one step to two.

exercises.title: Application Visualization
exercises.meta: Solo · 5–10 min · Ten to the Tenth (full PDF)
exercises.body:
Visualize how you'd normally handle an upcoming situation. Run Ten to the Tenth, climb several octaves, and re-visualize the situation from the new state. Repeat until a satisfying strategy emerges, then push past it for a quantum shift.

The applied form of the Part III scale — a fit for negotiation prep (the Cyprus framing) and youth decision-making.

interludes.title: INTERLUDE — OPENING
interludes.text:
This second has passed
as has this one
The moment is so fleeting
yet
the now is eternal

Richard Moon

interludes.title: INTERLUDE — AFTER PART I
interludes.text:
Feel
into the center
of your central core
even by drops
in ever finer adjustments

Richard Moon

interludes.title: INTERLUDE — AFTER PART II
interludes.text:
Listen to the impulse to breathe
follow the guidance
breathe exactly
like you want to

Richard Moon

interludes.title: INTERLUDE — AFTER PART III
interludes.text:
I don't really study Aikido as a Martial art,
an art in the realm of Mars, the god of war.
I study Aikido as a Venusial art,
an art in the realm of Venus, the goddess of love.

Richard Moon

interludes.title: INTERLUDE — CLOSING
interludes.text:
joy is the greatest treasure
don't get mad
don't even get even
create a beautiful world

Richard Moon

“Love gives birth to harmony, harmony brings forth joy, and joy is the greatest treasure.” — Morihei Ueshiba, O-Sensei.
